dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hi, Lorraine. Yeah, I'm calling about my street. It's Wednesday and it's still basically a skating rink. Which I assume wasn't the plan.
Oh, I'm sorry about that. Which street are you on? And is it a city street or a private way, do you know?
Um, I'd rather not give the house number, if that's all right. It's Harrison Avenue, out toward the end past the little park. It's a city street. Got a city sign and everything.
Okay, Harrison Avenue, out past the park. That's fine, I can log it by the street. And tell me what you're seeing out there.

So the snow came Sunday, turned to rain Monday, and then everything froze solid Monday night. Now it's a sheet of ice, curb to curb. No bare spots. I watched a guy in a pickup go down the hill about two miles an hour, sideways.
Sideways, wow. So it's not really snow anymore, it's glazed over. Ice from the rain freezing on top of what was left.
Right. The plow came through Sunday night, I'll give them that. Pushed everything to the side. But nobody's put down sand or salt since. It needs sand or salt. Something. Anything with grit in it.
Understood. Let me repeat that back so I have it right. Harrison Avenue past the park, solid ice since Monday night, plowed Sunday but no sand or salt applied since. Is that about it?
That's it. You nailed it.
Is there a hill or a curve there? Crews sometimes work the steep spots and intersections first, so it helps to know.
There's a decent slope right where it meets the cross street. That's where the pickup guy was. And my mailbox has seen better days, so, you know, I'm invested.
Okay. I'll note the slope at the cross street. Do you know if anyone's been hurt or any cars slid into anything?
Not that I've seen. A neighbor's trash can went for a ride. That's about the extent of it so far.
Good, that's good. So I'll put this in as an icy road request and flag the slope.
Okay. So when's it getting done? Like, am I looking at today, or should I just put cleats on the dog?

[pause] Let me look at the sheet here. The crews have been working the main roads and the hills first since Monday night, and the side streets come after. I'd say you're looking at sometime this afternoon into this evening for a sanding truck. Could slide to tomorrow morning if they get tied up.
This afternoon into tomorrow. So, a range. A wide range.
It's a wide one, I know. With the temperature right around freezing today, they're hoping some of it softens up on its own, but I wouldn't count on that on a side street in the shade.
Yeah, mine's all shade. Big trees, no sun. The ice is going to outlast me.
Then I'll make a note that it's shaded and not likely to melt. That helps them prioritize. Do you want a call back when it's been treated, or just to leave it with me?
Eh, a call back isn't necessary. I'll know when it's done. I'll hear the truck. Or I'll stop hearing people swear.
Fair enough. I won't take your number then. Is there anything else going on in the neighborhood, like a sidewalk issue or a drain?
No, just the road. Sidewalks, I gave up on those. I'm walking in the street like a rebel.
Please be careful out there, though. If you do have to walk, stay off the slope if you can.

Yeah, will do. Hey, unrelated, sort of. My power's been flickering and the house is a little cold, so I was looking at space heaters. Found a coupon online for forty percent off one. Figured that's the one good thing to come out of this week.
Well, that's something. Forty percent is a nice discount. Just make sure you plug it right into the wall and not an extension cord, and keep it clear of curtains and stuff.
Good tip. Right into the wall. I'll be responsible. Boring, but responsible.

Boring is safe. Okay, so let me read it one more time for the crew. Harrison Avenue past the park, icy, shaded, steep at the cross street, needs sand or salt, reported Wednesday around noon. Did I get everything?
You did. Nothing to add. Thanks for taking it down.
Of course. Hopefully they get to you this afternoon. If it's still bare ice tomorrow morning, call back and we'll push it again.
Will do. I appreciate it, Lorraine. Have a good one.
You too, Mr. Brito. Stay upright.
Doing my best. Bye.
